content.comment_body: I have a new computer with Windows 8 and [product_name] version 7 installed, available in both 32-bit and 64-bit. Both versions only install under Windows XP compatibility mode, but they function after installation. However, the USB cable does not work, and I get a warning about installing a 32-bit version on a 64-bit system. How can I resolve this and get the system working?

Hello, [product_name] is not officially released for Windows 8 yet. For which operating systems is [product_name] available? You can try suggestions from this forum thread, but it will be without official support from [company_name]. Regards,
Hi, [user_name], you installed the USB cable drivers in Windows 8.

I installed the drivers from [company_name] to use the USB cable, but it doesn't work. The installation looks fine, but I get error messages when using the cable in [product_name] under Extra > Options > Interface. Sorry for my English, it's not very good.

Hi, the USB cable driver included on the [product_name] installation DVD does not support Windows 8. Go to the installation folder for [product_name] and check the information about the USB cable driver. It may be made by Siliconlabs. Visit their website and look for a Windows 8-compatible driver. I don't have personal experience, but this seems like the best option. Hope this helps.

No, actually, the USB cable driver from the [product_name] DVD does support Windows 8/64-bit. Install 'CP210x_VCP_Win2K_XP_S2K3_Vista.exe' from the DVD and update the driver in Windows 8. You should be able to find the COM port, such as COM5.

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced compatibility problems between Windows 8 and the USB cable driver required for [product_name] V7. The software would install using XP compatibility mode, but USB functionality failed due to warnings about 32-bit drivers on 64-bit systems. Some advised that the DVD drivers were incompatible, while others stated they actually work with Windows 8/64-bit. Uncertainty and a lack of official support for Windows 8 resulted in confusion and frustration for users trying to use the product on newer computers.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect immediate compatibility of [company_name] software and hardware with Windows 8, seeking plug-and-play functionality without extra driver installations or workarounds. They want easy connection between their devices and the software.
